answer: In an AI-agent marketplace for ferrous scrap, velvet, and nectar, every bidding identity must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before receiving one daily auction slot. Splitting into 1,000 identities therefore requires locking $100,000, not merely generating keys. The fixed lock prevents recycling one bond through many names during that period, so extra auction influence costs the attacker proportional capital and its foregone yield.
